articles.title: Newscast - Can The Chancellor's Positive Vibes Limit Tax Rises? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey aims for ‘vibes boost’ in first major economic speech.
articles.body: Today, John Healey delivered his first major speech as chancellor, aiming to boost confidence in the economy with a positive message. The chancellor set out his intentions for growth, investment and more jobs. But midway through, Jaguar Land Rover announced they would be making thousands of job cuts after struggling with competition from China and falling behind in the electric vehicle race. Economics editor Faisal Islam and business editor Simon Jack explain what it means for the country, and they chat through Healey’s new ‘Make Great Britain Growth Britain Again” And we've had a weekend of anti-migration protests. One involved men in balaclavas in Dover and one with a crowd trying to block the migrant coaches in Portsmouth. UK correspondent Daniel Sandford explains. You can now listen to Newscast on a smart speaker. If you want to listen, just say "Ask BBC Sounds to play Newscast”. It works on most smart speakers. If you're in the UK, for more News and Current Affairs podcasts from the BBC, listen on BBC Sounds: Newscast brings you daily analysis of the latest political news stories from the BBC. The presenter was Adam Fleming. It was made by Jack Maclaren with Anna Harris and Lois Worrow. The social producer was Gabriel Purcell-Davis. The technical producer was Philip Bull and Holly Smith. articles.summary: Should the league be supporting home grown talent more?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 07 Sep 2026 , · 42 mins

Ben and Ellen are joined by The Guardian's Tom Garry as the WSL returns! Kick off times have changed this season, what is the best time for a women's football audience to have games played? Is the Sunday evening match a good idea and who does it appeal to most? Elsewhere London City Lionesses started strongly with some of the biggest global stars in their line up, however none of their starting XI were English. Tom and Ellen debate what this means for football in England and the development of the game. Should the league be doing more to help home grown talent? Plus an investigation is under way after Crystal Palace breached a rule by using four substitution windows in their 1-0 win over Everton. articles.title: Merz se diz 'profundamente chocado' após vitória da AfD | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder alemão reconheceu que seu partido sofreu "a mais grave derrota eleitoral em décadas", mas se disse determinado a prosseguir caminho de reformas. "Desistir não é uma opção para mim", afirmou.
articles.summary: Líder alemão reconheceu que seu partido sofreu "a mais grave derrota eleitoral em décadas", mas se disse determinado a prosseguir caminho de reformas. "Desistir não é uma opção para mim", afirmou.
articles.body:
O chanceler alemão e líder da União Democrata-Cristã (CDU), Friedrich Merz, participa de entrevista coletiva em Berlim, um dia após as eleições estaduais na Saxônia-Anhalt, nesta segunda-feira (7). — Foto: REUTERS/Axel Schmidt

O chanceler federal alemão, Friedrich Merz, declarou nesta segunda-feira (07/09), estar "profundamente chocado" com a derrota avassaladora sofrida por seu partido, a União Democrata Cristã (CDU), frente à legenda de ultradireita Alternativa para a Alemanha (AfD) nas eleições regionais realizadas no dia anterior no estado de Saxônia-Anhalt.

"Desde ontem, não apenas a Saxônia-Anhalt mudou, mas toda a Alemanha", afirmou Merz, após reuniões com lideranças da CDU em Berlim. "Esse resultado eleitoral terá consequências", assegurou.

Merz admitiu que seus baixos índices de popularidade nas pesquisas contribuíram para a derrota de seu partido: "Sei que eu, pessoalmente, fui um tema constante nesta campanha eleitoral", disse ele.

O chanceler informou que conversará nos próximos dias com o parceiro de coalizão, o Partido Social-Democrata (SPD) e ressaltou que o rumo das reformas adotado pelo governo está correto em seus princípios. No entanto, deixou claro que está disposto a discutir aspectos específicos da reforma da previdência, bem como o volume da reforma tributária.

"Minha determinação em prosseguir com o caminho de reformas permanece inabalada", afirmou o líder conservador, ressalvando, contudo, que tentaria explicar "melhor" aos eleitores o programa de reformas do governo, destacando que elas não são um fim em si mesmas, mas um instrumento para atingir objetivos concretos.

Merz ainda classificou o resultado em Sachsen-Anhalt como a "mais dura derrota eleitoral da CDU em décadas" – seu partido obteve apenas 17,2 % dos votos (20 pontos a menos em relação ao último pleito no estado) frente a 43,8 % da AfD, que mais que dobrou frente a seu resultado anterior.

Oresultado negativo elevou a pressão sobre Merz, não apenas por parte da ultradireita, mas também de dentro de sua coalizão, que tem enfrentado dificuldades para reaquecer uma economia estagnada e está dividida em questões de política social, especialmente no que diz respeito às aposentadorias.

Ao assumir a liderança do governo alemão em 2025, Merz prometeu reconduzir a CDU às suas raízes conservadoras e iniciou medidas rigorosas contra a imigração irregular enquanto tenta recuperar a economia, mas seus índices de popularidade permanecem baixos.

Nesta segunda-feira, Merz disse não ver motivos para enfrentar consequências pessoais após as pesadas perdas de seu partido. "Desistir não é uma opção para mim", frisou. Ele afirmou ser responsabilidade do governo federal — e sua própria responsabilidade pessoal — "criar oportunidades para a próxima geração agora". Filhos e netos devem, segundo ele, ter a mesma chance que a sua geração de viver em liberdade, paz e prosperidade. "Essa é a responsabilidade, e não estou fugindo dela", acrescentou Merz.

Ele recordou que em duas semanas ocorrerão eleições regionais em Berlim e em Mecklemburgo-Pomerânia Ocidental e que, após esses pleitos, será realizada uma análise em seu partido e em sua coalizão de governo sobre o que pode ser feito de maneira diferente.

articles.title: Propaganda pró-Rússia usa militares ucranianas como isca | G1
articles.standfirst: Canais ussos no Telegram usam falsas acusações de estupro e imagem de mulheres ucranianas para atrair milhões de usuários a redes de propaganda favoráveis à guerra.
articles.summary: Canais ussos no Telegram usam falsas acusações de estupro e imagem de mulheres ucranianas para atrair milhões de usuários a redes de propaganda favoráveis à guerra.
articles.body:
Keti Leshkasheli descobriu que sua imagem estava sendo usada para atrair usuários a canais pró-Rússia — Foto: Keti Leshkasheli via BBC

Aviso: esta reportagem contém conteúdo que alguns leitores podem considerar perturbador.

Quando Keti Leshkasheli, médica da Geórgia que serviu nas Forças Armadas da Ucrânia , voltou da linha de frente, há cerca de três anos, seu celular não parava de vibrar.

Amigos e familiares queriam saber se ela estava bem. Eles haviam visto publicações no aplicativo de mensagens Telegram que afirmavam que Leshkasheli tinha sido capturada e estuprada.

"Fiquei sabendo que havia aparecido um vídeo dizendo que algumas garotas e eu tínhamos sido capturadas. Havia um link para um canal no Telegram que mostrava como estávamos sendo 'punidas'", contou Leshkasheli à BBC.

Ela se reconheceu na imagem. Era uma foto dela, tirada anos antes, em que aparece de uniforme militar em Avdiivka, cidade no leste da Ucrânia que hoje está sob ocupação russa.

Leshkasheli serviu como paramédica militar na Legião Internacional da Ucrânia e foi condecorada pelo presidente Volodymyr Zelensky em 2025 — Foto: Keti Leshkasheli via BBC

"Escreveram todo tipo de horror sobre mim", explicou. "Me dá raiva. Não posso fazer nada a respeito."

A publicação fazia parte de uma grande rede de anúncios enganosos no Telegram. Eles usavam alegações falsas de que mulheres ucranianas haviam sido estupradas, acompanhadas de vídeos que comprovariam os abusos, para atrair usuários a canais pró-Rússia.

O Serviço Mundial da BBC identificou imagens de mais de 20 mulheres — muitas delas integrantes ou ex-integrantes do Exército ucraniano — usadas como isca para cliques nessa campanha. A BBC conversou com sete delas.

Desde que a Rússia invadiu a Ucrânia, em fevereiro de 2022, milhares de publicações em grupos ou canais do Telegram prometeram mostrar imagens de prisioneiras de guerra ucranianas sendo estupradas e executadas.

O Telegram é um aplicativo de mensagens no qual os usuários entram em grandes canais ou grupos para compartilhar e discutir conteúdos.

As publicações nesses espaços costumam incluir anúncios com links para outros canais, grupos privados ou sites externos.

A plataforma é especialmente eficaz para atrair público, já que é o aplicativo de mensagens mais popular na Rússia. Em 2025, também foi uma das principais fontes de notícias para os ucranianos, segundo uma pesquisa nacional.

Ao analisar frases recorrentes e nomes falsos usados nessas publicações no Telegram, o Serviço Mundial da BBC encontrou mais de 6,5 mil anúncios com alegações de violência sexual.

Esses anúncios haviam sido publicados por cerca de 1,7 mil canais de pequeno porte, dedicados a temas variados, como conteúdo para maiores de 18 anos, material favorável à guerra, finanças e memes.

Juntas, essas publicações acumularam mais de 65 milhões de visualizações.

A maioria seguia a mesma fórmula: usava fotos reais de mulheres, afirmava falsamente que elas haviam sido sequestradas e estupradas e incluía um link que prometia mostrar provas em vídeo.

Era uma tática deliberadamente chocante, criada para atrair público com a promessa de mostrar imagens perturbadoras.

As publicações também afirmavam que as mulheres haviam torturado soldados russos ou "defendido que crianças russas fossem queimadas vivas". Essas alegações vinham acompanhadas de insultos étnicos e de gênero.

Mas, quando o usuário acessava as publicações, o conteúdo prometido não existia. Em vez disso, os links levavam a canais privados do Telegram repletos de conteúdo favorável à guerra.

Essas publicações também circulam fora do Telegram. Vídeos no TikTok e no YouTube, assim como publicações na rede social russa VKontakte, prometem o mesmo conteúdo enquanto promovem os mesmos canais privados do Telegram.

Valentyna Shapovalova, pesquisadora que estuda desinformação de gênero, afirma que a campanha "vende a promessa de violência sexualizada como entretenimento" para "atrair e monetizar" a atenção dos usuários.

A Rússia lançou uma onde de ataques com drones e mísseis balísticos em 31 de agosto, matando pelo menos 12 pessoas — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Shapovalova acrescenta que, mesmo quando não são produzidas pelo Estado, essas publicações ainda contribuem para os objetivos de guerra da Rússia, porque humilham os ucranianos e "normalizam a violência sexual contra o 'inimigo'".

Ao identificar padrões e mapear as conexões entre as publicações, a BBC rastreou uma rede de canais que se beneficia dessa campanha para atrair seguidores. Seis canais ultrapassaram a marca de 1 milhão de inscritos.

A BBC analisou três dos maiores. Todos foram criados em um intervalo de 72 horas entre si, no início da invasão russa em grande escala, em fevereiro de 2022.

O Pryamoy Efir Novosti, canal associado a mais de 1 mil das publicações analisadas pela BBC, tem hoje mais de 4 milhões de inscritos — mais do que a maioria dos principais comentaristas pró-Rússia e muitos veículos de comunicação estatais.

O canal se apresenta como um veículo de notícias, mas originalmente se chamava "MVD 18+", em uma referência a conteúdo adulto.

A maior parte de seu histórico de mensagens, referente ao período em que a campanha para atrair seguidores estava mais ativa, desapareceu.

Hoje, o canal funciona como qualquer outro agregador de notícias pró-Rússia no Telegram. Publica dezenas de vezes por dia, usa veículos estatais russos como fonte e vende publicidade ao Alfa-Bank, um dos maiores bancos privados na Rússia, alvo de sanções do Reino Unido, da União Europeia e dos Estados Unidos.

O Alfa-Bank não respondeu ao pedido de comentário da BBC.

Os três canais reproduzem conteúdo da mídia estatal russa e seguem a linha do Kremlin, governo russo. Descrevem avanços militares como "libertações", apresentam a União Europeia e o Reino Unido como agressores e celebram as baixas ucranianas. Dois deles usam regularmente insultos étnicos contra ucranianos.

Para descobrir quanto esses canais lucram com conteúdo favorável à guerra, a BBC entrou em contato com eles se passando por um possível anunciante.

O Pryamoy Efir Novosti informou que cobra no mínimo 500 mil rublos (R$ 29,9 mil) por anúncio. Os outros dois, que publicam insultos e conteúdo violento, disseram cobrar cerca de 40 mil rublos (R$ 2.400) cada.

O Pryamoy Efir não respondeu a nenhuma das perguntas da BBC. Em uma mensagem, o canal chamou a BBC de "provocadora e propagandista" e afirmou que as informações "não correspondem à realidade".

Das mais de 6,5 mil publicações enganosas usadas para atrair cliques identificadas pela BBC, quase 5,4 mil foram removidas desde então.

Mas novas publicações continuam surgindo. Algumas apresentam sinais de automação: textos idênticos, inclusive com os mesmos erros de digitação, publicados simultaneamente em várias contas.

"Denunciei essas contas e as bloqueei, mas são muitas", disse Yuliia Mala. "O número dessas contas falsas não para de crescer."

Lesia Palahniuk, conselheira regional de Chernivtsi, cidade no oeste da Ucrânia, se reconheceu em publicações que circulavam em canais russos no Telegram — Foto: Lesia Palahniuk via BBC

As denúncias formais feitas pelas mulheres cujas imagens foram usadas em publicações violentas tiveram, em grande parte, pouco efeito.

Leshkasheli disse ter feito várias denúncias ao Telegram. "É quase impossível fazer alguma coisa", lamentou. "Quero que as pessoas saibam que esse tipo de fraude existe e não caiam nessa armadilha."

Oleksandra, cidadã russa que se ofereceu como voluntária para lutar pela Ucrânia, disse ter visto publicações com suas fotos em 2022, 2023 e 2024 em tantos canais que acabou deixando de acompanhá-las.

"Vi que usavam minhas fotos e que colocavam digitalmente meu rosto sobre um corpo nu... Havia tanto conteúdo assim que, em determinado momento, parei de reagir", disse Oleksandra.

O Telegram não respondeu ao pedido de comentário da BBC.

Desde fevereiro de 2026, o órgão regulador de mídia da Rússia restringe o Telegram no país, sob a acusação de que a plataforma não cumpre a legislação russa.

A medida, no entanto, teve pouco efeito sobre o uso do aplicativo, já que os russos recorrem a VPNs (sigla em inglês para "rede privada virtual") para acessar a plataforma.

Lesia Palahniuk, conselheira regional de Chernivtsi cuja foto foi usada em publicações com linguagem obscena, afirmou que esse tipo de exposição faz com que as mulheres carreguem uma vergonha que não lhes pertence.

"Para uma mulher, ver fotos assim é muito difícil", afirmou Palahniuk. "As mulheres precisam saber que não estão sozinhas, que têm apoio. Elas não fizeram nada de errado."

articles.title: Homem é arrastado por enxurrada e fica preso em bueiro em Goiás | G1
articles.standfirst: Morador de Valparaíso de Goiás, Luciano Rufino da Costa ficou preso com apenas os braços e a cabeça para fora. O motoboy Luan Silva Araújo conseguiu retirar o homem do bueiro com a ajuda do cunhado.
articles.summary: Luciano Rufino da Costa, de 49 anos, foi arrastado pela enxurrada e ficou preso em um bueiro durante temporal em Valparaíso de Goiás. Dois homens fizeram o resgate.
articles.body:
O morador de Valparaíso de Goiás , na região do Entorno do Distrito Federal, Luciano Rufino da Costa, de 49 anos, ficou com parte do corpo preso em um bueiro após ser arrastado por uma enxurrada durante um temporal no domingo (6). Segundo apuração da TV Anhanguera, o pior não aconteceu porque dois homens que passavam pelo local de carro conseguiram resgatá-lo e levá-lo para um local seguro (veja o vídeo).

Segundo a reportagem, a rua onde fica o bueiro tem uma forte descida, por onde a água da chuva desagua. Em entrevista à TV, o motoboy Luan Silva Araújo contou que voltava de um almoço em família quando avistou Luciano apenas com a cabeça e os braços para fora do bueiro. Ele disse que a esposa chegou a pensar que fossem crianças brincando na enxurrada, mas, ao reduzir a velocidade do veículo, o motoboy viu Luciano preso no bueiro e, com a ajuda do cunhado, realizou o resgate.

"Parei o carro imediatamente, meu cunhado desceu e nós o tiramos de lá. Perguntamos o que tinha acontecido e ele contou que a enxurrada o havia arrastado", disse ele.

Sobre o resgate, o jovem explicou que a ação precisou ser rápida devido às condições da enxurrada. Segundo ele, o volume de água batia diretamente no rosto da vítima, em meio à lama e às pedras trazidas pela chuva.

"Havia muita água batendo no rosto dele, além de barro e pedras. Ele saiu bem, mas estava com os braços fracos por ter ficado preso lutando contra a correnteza", completou.

Luciano Rufino da Costa ficou preso em um bueiro após ser arrastado por uma enxurrada em Valparaíso de Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

articles.title: Frio e chuva devem continuar na região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Cássia dos Coqueiros registrou a menor temperatura da região nesta segunda-feira (7). Chuva deve se intensificar até o fim da semana.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo para Ribeirão Preto e Franca indica que o frio é passageiro, mas a chuva ganha força com acumulados significativos ao longo desta semana.
articles.body:
A mudança no tempo derrubou as temperaturas nesta segunda-feira (7) na região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca (SP), mas quem tirou os casacos do armário não deve se acostumar. O frio é passageiro e, ao longo da semana, os termômetros voltam a subir. A chuva, por outro lado, deve aparecer com frequência nos próximos dias.

Nesta segunda-feira, Cássia dos Coqueiros (SP) registrou 10°C, a menor temperatura entre as cidades da região. A sensação térmica ficou ainda mais baixa por causa da chuva durante a manhã.

Em Ribeirão Preto, os termômetros marcavam 19°C no início da tarde e a máxima não deveria passar dos 20°C. Barretos tinha previsão de máxima de 20°C, enquanto Franca poderia chegar aos 22°C.

Massa de ar polar causou firo e chuva na regi — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

No sábado (5), rajadas de vento chegaram a 65 km/h na região . Depois da ventania, vieram a chuva e o ar polar, responsáveis pela mudança no tempo.

A queda nas temperaturas é resultado da combinação entre a passagem da frente fria e a chegada de uma massa de ar polar. O céu encoberto e os ventos vindos do Sul do país também ajudaram a manter o frio.

Apesar disso, a frente fria já está se afastando da região. A tendência é de tempo mais firme durante a noite desta segunda, mas a instabilidade não vai embora com ela.

Isso acontece porque um cavado — uma área alongada de baixa pressão atmosférica que favorece a formação de nuvens e chuva — começa a atuar e deve manter a possibilidade de precipitações durante a semana.

A massa de ar polar perde força nos próximos dias e, com isso, as temperaturas começam a subir novamente.

Em Ribeirão Preto, depois do frio desta segunda-feira, a previsão indica máxima de 24°C na terça-feira (8), 28°C na quarta-feira (9) e 29°C na quinta-feira (10).

A elevação das temperaturas, porém, não significa uma sequência de tempo seco. Na terça, há previsão de chuva, e na quinta os acumulados podem chegar a 17 milímetros.

A tendência, portanto, é de uma semana de "gangorra" nos termômetros, com alternância entre períodos mais frios e mais quentes.

Ao contrário do frio, pontual, a instabilidade pode permanecer por mais tempo neste mês.

Além da atuação do cavado durante a semana, uma nova frente fria deve se formar no Sul do país no fim de semana e pode aumentar novamente a chuva na região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca.

A previsão aponta a probabilidade de um acumulado de até 97 milímetros nos próximos 13 dias.

O inverno termina no dia 21 de setembro.

articles.title: Negociações de paz: Kremlin admite retomar diálogo com Ucrânia e EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Após reuniões de enviados dos EUA com Putin e Zelensky, Moscou mantém aberta a possibilidade de novas negociações de paz, mas diz ser cedo para definir data e local de um novo encontro.
articles.summary: Porta-voz admite retomar negociações de paz com Ucrânia e EUA após missão diplomática americana, mas afirma ser cedo para definir data e local de um novo encontro.
articles.body:
Dmitry Peskov, porta-voz do Kremlin, durante discurso na última sexta (18) — Foto: Sputnik/Sergey Guneev/Kremlin via REUTERS

O Kremlin afirmou nesta segunda-feira (7) que não descarta a retomada das negociações de paz entre Rússia, Ucrânia e Estados Unidos, mas ressaltou que ainda é cedo para definir quando e onde um novo encontro poderá ocorrer, apesar da intensificação dos contatos diplomáticos nos últimos dias.

A declaração foi feita pelo porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, após a visita dos enviados americanos Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner a Moscou e Kiev .

A dupla busca destravar as negociações para um acordo que encerre a guerra na Ucrânia.

Segundo Peskov, Moscou também não descarta uma conversa por telefone entre o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, e o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, para discutir os resultados da missão diplomática dos enviados.

O porta-voz afirmou, porém, que o Kremlin ainda não recebeu informações sobre as reuniões realizadas pelos representantes americanos com autoridades ucranianas em Kiev no domingo (6).

Ucrânia diz que propostas continuam construtivas

O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, recebe Jared Kushner e o enviado especial dos EUA Steve Witkoff em Kiev, neste domingo (6). — Foto: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters

Em uma publicação na rede social X, o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, informou que realizou uma reunião com a equipe de negociação após os encontros com os enviados do presidente dos EUA em Kiev.

Segundo Zelensky, foram realizadas três rodadas de negociações, com a participação de representantes do E3 — França, Reino Unido e Alemanha.

Ele acrescentou que também teve uma conversa reservada com os enviados americanos Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner para discutir os resultados do dia.

"O mais importante é continuar trabalhando juntos, de forma ativa, para manter a diplomacia em andamento", escreveu.

O presidente ucraniano afirmou que as conversas abordaram as necessidades do país em defesa aérea, a cooperação tecnológica e o pacote de apoio necessário para o inverno.

Segundo ele, os parceiros internacionais sabem quais medidas podem produzir resultados antes da chegada da estação.

Zelensky disse ainda que as próximas etapas já estão sendo coordenadas e que novas reuniões e contatos diplomáticos estão sendo preparados. "As propostas da Ucrânia são construtivas e continuarão sendo", concluiu.

articles.title: Campineiros enfrentam frio para acompanhar desfile de 7 de Setembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Com temperatura de 14°C, evento reuniu cerca de 20 mil pessoas e contou com tropas das Forças Armadas, PM, Bombeiros, escolas e fanfarras.
articles.summary: Com temperatura de 14°C, evento reuniu cerca de 20 mil pessoas e contou com tropas das Forças Armadas, PM, Bombeiros, escolas e fanfarras.
articles.body:
As baixas temperaturas não impediram que milhares de pessoas acompanhassem os desfiles cívico-militares do Dia da Independência, neste feriado de 7 de Setembro, em Campinas (SP).

Mesmo com os termômetros marcando 14°C, com sensação térmica ainda menor devido ao vento, o evento reuniu cerca de 20 mil espectadores, segundo a prefeitura.

Na Avenida Francisco Glicério, no Centro, a programação foi dividida em duas etapas.

O evento começou com a exibição de veículos históricos usados na Segunda Guerra Mundial, seguida pelo desfile de tropas do Exército, Polícia Militar, Corpo de Bombeiros e sobrevoo do helicóptero Águia.

A segunda parte contou com escolas, fanfarras e entidades assistenciais, sendo encerrada pelo Grito dos Excluídos.

Desfile de 7 de Setembro reuniu 20 mil pessoas na região central de Campinas (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

articles.title: VÍDEOS: Bom Dia Tocantins de segunda-feira, 7 de setembro de 2026
articles.summary: VÍDEOS: Bom Dia Tocantins de segunda-feira, 7 de setembro de 2026

articles.title: Barco com passageiros afunda no rio Tocantins, em Marabá, no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Naufrágio aconteceu na tarde de domingo, 6, na região da Transmangueira. Outros barqueiros que passavam pelo local agiram rápido e resgataram as vítimas.
articles.summary: Naufrágio aconteceu na tarde de domingo, 6, na região da Transmangueira. Outros barqueiros que passavam pelo local agiram rápido e resgataram as vítimas.
articles.body:
Um barco de pequeno porte que transportava vários passageiros naufragou nas águas do Rio Tocantins, na tarde de domingo (6), em Marabá , no sudeste do Pará. Todas as pessoas que estavam a bordo foram retiradas da água em segurança.

O naufrágio aconteceu na altura da região conhecida como Transmangueira e assustou banhistas e moradores que passavam pelo local.

O momento exato em que a embarcação começa a submergir foi registrado em vídeo por testemunhas que estavam às margens do rio.

Embarcação com passageiros naufraga no rio Tocantins, em Marabá. — Foto: Reprodução / Rede sociais

Nas imagens, que circulam nas redes sociais, é possível ver o desespero das pessoas enquanto o barco afunda rapidamente na água.

Apesar da gravidade do acidente, a ação rápida de outros barqueiros que trabalham na região evitou que o naufrágio terminasse em tragédia.

Ao presenciarem a embarcação afundando, os pilotos de outros barcos se deslocaram imediatamente até o ponto do naufrágio e iniciaram o resgate dos passageiros.

Não houve registro de pessoas feridas ou desaparecidas. As causas que levaram ao naufrágio da embarcação ainda estão sendo apuradas.

articles.title: Duas pessoas morrem após caminhão atingir veículos em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na Linha Verde, na manhã desta segunda-feira (7). Caminhão-tanque estava vazio.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu na Linha Verde, na manhã desta segunda-feira (7). Caminhão-tanque estava vazio.
articles.body:
Duas pessoas morreram após um caminhão-tanque atingir veículos que estavam parados para ajudar um motociclista que havia caído na Linha Verde, em Curitiba , nesta segunda-feira (7). O acidente aconteceu em um trecho de curva com a pista molhada.

Segundo apurou a RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, o motociclista perdeu o controle da moto ao fazer a curva e caiu na pista. Em seguida, alguns motoristas pararam para prestar ajuda.

Entre as pessoas que pararam estavam dois policiais militares. Eles chegaram a orientar que alguém subisse na via para sinalizar o acidente, porque o trecho era considerado perigoso. Pouco depois, porém, um caminhão-tanque que transportava combustível desceu a alça de acesso e não conseguiu frear.

O motociclista e uma pessoa que parou para ajudá-lo foram atingidos e morreram . A segunda vítima chegou a ser socorrida e encaminhada ao hospital, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Segundo informações da Guarda Municipal, responsável pela administração da Linha Verde, foram registrados 48 metros de frenagem antes da colisão.

Os PMs não se feriram. A dinâmica do acidente deve ser investigada.

Duas pessoas morrem após caminhão atingir veículos que pararam para ajudar motociclista caído na pista em Curitiba — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Em nota, a Transportadora Nichele, responsável pelo caminhão, lamentou o acidente e manifestou solidariedade aos familiares das vítimas. A empresa informou que o veículo estava vazio, que não houve vazamento de combustível e que, até o momento, não foram identificados indícios de falha mecânica no sistema de frenagem.

"A Transportadora Nichele está colaborando integralmente com as autoridades competentes e disponibilizando as informações necessárias à apuração. A empresa aguardará a conclusão das análises técnicas antes de se manifestar sobre as causas ou responsabilidades pelo acidente", diz a nota.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reúne apoiadores e aliados políticos em ato na Avenida Paulista  | G1
articles.standfirst: Manifestação ocorre nesta segunda-feira (7), feriado de 7 de Setembro; Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) chegou ao ato por volta das 15h.
articles.summary: Manifestação ocorre nesta segunda-feira (7), feriado de 7 de Setembro; Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) chegou ao ato por volta das 15h.
articles.body:
Apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro durante ato na Avenida Paulista nesta segunda-feira (7) — Foto: TV Globo

O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reúne apoiadores na tarde desta segunda-feira (7) na Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo . O ato de campanha tem como mote as frases "Fora Lula, Fora Moraes".

Por volta das 13h30, grupos com bandeiras do Brasil e vestidos de camisetas amarelas começaram a se concentrar pela avenida. Apoiadores também chegaram com faixas contra o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), principalmente contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes.

O governador de São Paulo e candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), também participa da manifestação. Mais cedo, ele não participou do desfile cívico-militar de 7 de Setembro realizado no Sambódromo do Anhembi. O governador foi representado no evento pelo vice Felicio Ramuth (MDB).

O prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes (MDB), foi um dos primeiros que discursou pedindo votos para Flávio, Tarcísio, além de Guilherme Derrite (PP) e André do Prado (PL) para o Senado.

Derrite também participou do ato, ao lado de André do Prado, Sergio Moro (PL), candidato ao governo do Paraná, e de Valdemar Costa Neto, presidente do PL.

"Quero declarar a independência do Brasil a partir de 2027 contra o crime organizado no Brasil. Ou os criminosos mudam de país, ou serão presos ou neutralizados no Brasil. Ninguém aguenta mais", disse Derrite.

"Só tem um jeito. O Jair Bolsonaro vai ficar preso mais 10 anos se o Flávio não for eleito. Se o Flávio for eleito, Bolsonaro estará com a gente no dia seguinte. Estamos juntos para a vitória", ressaltou Valdemar.

Flávio Bolsonaro durante ato na Avenida Paulista — Foto: TV Globo

O ato ocorre após a repercussão de mensagens trocadas entre o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e o ministro do STF Alexandre de Moraes que apontam uma relação de proximidade entre o magistrado e o ex-controlador do Banco Master à época dos fatos investigados.

A manifestação também retoma uma pauta já presente em atos anteriores da direita. Em 2024, um protesto foi convocado com pedidos de impeachment de Moraes . No ano passado, manifestantes voltaram a defender a saída do ministro no ato da Paulista.

articles.title: Nepal flooding victims to get £50,000 of support from Guernsey
articles.summary: The States of Guernsey is giving the money to a Cornwall charity response team in Nepal.
articles.body:
Communities in Nepal impacted by fatal flash flooding will receive £50,000 worth of support funded by officials in Guernsey.

The island's government said its Overseas Aid & Development Commission had approved the funding, which would be given to Cornish-based charity Shelterbox's response team in Nepal.

More than 1,300 people have been reported dead in the country following flooding which struck near the border with Tibet on 26 August .

Commission president Jennifer Strachan said she was pleased to support Shelterbox's efforts to provide emergency shelter and essential household items to affected communities and families.

"Our thoughts and sympathies are with all those affected and we recognise the immense human suffering and hardship being experienced by communities across the region," she said.

Alex Orme, head of programme funding at international disaster for ShelterBox, said: "For those in Nepal who have lost their homes, livelihoods and loved ones, this money will fund lifesaving aid items that will help families to protect themselves from the elements as they begin the difficult task of rebuilding their lives.

"With thousands of homes damaged or completely destroyed, the need for shelter has never been more urgent and donations such as this will enable us to work with local partners to provide emergency shelter and essential aid items such as blankets, sleeping mats, solar lights and kitchen sets, to those who need it most."

Orme said the "right help" could "help to restore dignity, stability and hope to vulnerable communities when disasters strike without warning".

"As Nepal moves from the immediate rescue phase of this disaster into the next stage of humanitarian response, attention is turning to the urgent needs of families who have lost their homes, possessions and access to essential services," Strachan said.

She added Shelterbox was a well-established partner of the commission and had received previous emergency relief funding for other humanitarian crises.

articles.title: How homeowners should prepare for ‘supersized’ El Niño this winter
articles.summary: “Don’t wait until the winter storms begin. Prepare now,” experts warn. First step if at risk? Get flood insurance.
articles.body:
Meteorologists are warning of a "supersized" El Niño potentially bringing heavy rains and flooding to the U.S. in the coming months, with those living in coastal areas facing the greater risks.

Fueled by exceptionally warm temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, El Niño , a recurring climate phenomenon resulting from variations in ocean temperatures in the Equatorial Pacific, is set to become "very strong" this fall and winter , according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

"El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up," United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement last week.

Communities across the U.S. are likely to feel the impact of what is expected to be the largest El Niño in at least 1,000 years, which promises to make 2027 an even hotter year than this one – and likely the hottest ever recorded, as climate scientist Gavin Schmidt warned.

What will happen next remains unclear, as "no two El Niños are exactly the same," Scott Handel, lead meteorologist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center, told Newsweek . But given the expected strength of this El Niño event, we can get a pretty good idea of what might occur.

"Much of the West Coast, especially California, has increased chances of heavy precipitation and flooding," Handel said. "Our last El Niño of 2023-24 produced record rainfall for San Diego in late January, and the El Niño of 1997-98 produced the wettest February on record for Los Angeles and San Francisco."

"Above-average temperatures are more likely across the Upper Midwest and much of the Northern Tier of the U.S. more generally," he added. "The Southeast is more prone to heavy rain, flooding, and severe weather. The Northern Rockies and northern Cascades tend to experience a reduced snowpack."

What U.S. Homeowners Should Know About El Niño

Heavy rain and flooding – which is a concern both for the West Coast and the Southeast, according to Handel – can be particularly devastating for homeowners on the path of destruction.

Handel explained: "Heavy rain and flooding could produce mudslides in vulnerable terrain across much of the West Coast and surrounding areas. Increased storminess may produce episodes of high winds along parts of the West Coast. Severe weather risks may be elevated for parts of the Southeast. The East Coast is more prone to coastal storms.

"None of these potential weather events are guaranteed, but homeowners should be prepared for elevated risks of impacts."

The most common property insurance claims during an El Niño winter include wind and roof damage from stronger, more frequent Pacific storms, according to Mark Friedlander, senior director of media relations at the Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I).

"Additionally, we see water damage and burst pipes from atypical cold snaps in the South and flooding from heavier-than-normal rainfall in California and along the Gulf Coast from Texas to Florida," Friedlander told Newsweek .

Tree and debris damage from high winds is common across numerous regions, Friedlander added, and "winter storm and freeze losses also tend to spike in areas unaccustomed to sustained cold snaps."

What Experts Suggest Homeowners Do To Prepare

Friedlander urges homeowners to be prepared for flood damage, which requires a separate policy from the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or a private flood insurer – something that many Americans lack.

Despite the growing frequency of severity of flooding across the country, with nearly every U.S. county having experienced flooding in the past few decades, only 4 percent of homeowners nationwide had flood insurance as of 2025, according to the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

The nation's flood insurance gap stems partly from the fact that many homeowners can no longer afford additional coverage after years of rising premiums. But it is also driven by a persistent belief that their properties are not at risk of flooding, a misconception that recent disasters have increasingly exposed.

"FEMA has noted that over the past decade almost one-third of flood insurance claims from the National Flood Insurance Program came from structures outside currently mapped high-risk flood areas. Structures in low-lying areas may be particularly vulnerable," Denali Pinto, research data analyst at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego, told Newsweek . "To find out your risk, you can search online for 'what is my flood zone' and enter your address at FEMA's Map Service Center."

He added: "It can flood anywhere it rains, not just in high-risk zones. Earth movement and landslide damage, which often accompanies saturated soil in heavy-rain events, is typically covered by a difference in conditions policy but may be restricted in high-risk landslide areas like California.

"Sewer and drain backup is important for homeowners that can be easily added as an endorsement to your standard home policy."

Homeowners who do not already have a separate policy for flood damage should contact their insurance agent and secure a policy "now given the standard 30-day NFIP waiting period," Friedlander said, adding: "With a potential federal government shutdown at the end of September, we recommend purchasing coverage immediately as new NFIP policies will not be available during a shutdown."

In terms of prevention, Pinto said: "If you know your property is prone to flooding, then be ready with sandbags ahead of big storms. Also, clear out your gutters and any drainage near your home.

"It's also good practice to keep a few days of food and water ready for emergencies and a large powerbank for charging electronics if the power or water goes out. Pay attention to the forecasts, and never drive into moving water on roadways, even if it seems fairly shallow. It could also be a good idea to purchase a NOAA weather radio to get weather updates even if the power goes out."

In general, "measures like portable flood barriers, increasing defensible space around homes to resist wildfires, and installing hurricane tie-downs on roofs may be very cost-effective," Ed Kearns, Managing Director and Head of Physical Risk Research & Development at First Street, part of MSCI, told Newsweek .

"Other measures, such as elevating home foundations, installing active fire suppression systems on rooftops, or entirely replacing roofs are typically much more expensive and should be carefully considered," he added.

If these preventative measures can stop the flood waters from entering the home, or avoiding igniting in a wildfire during the drier season, or the roof stays on intact during a hurricane – that would mean essentially zeroing the potential losses caused by something like a strong El Niño.

"Again, the user should consider the costs of implementation versus the potential losses for their structure," Kearns said.

Homeowners in areas at risk should also create a home inventory and document belongings and property with photos and/or video, Friedlander recommended, as a detailed home inventory can help expedite claims filing.

"Additionally, clear gutters, drains and storm drains near your property, review evacuation routes and have emergency supplies on hand (at least seven-day supplies of non-perishable food and water – 1 gallon per person per day – and medications), and a 'go bag' with essential supplies and important documents in case of an urgent evacuation," Friedlander said, adding: "Don't wait until the winter storms begin. Prepare now."

Which Parts of the Country Should Be on Alert

"The biggest risks will be tied to where the storm track sets up and how active it becomes," Crystal Egger, President of Monarch Weather Consulting, told Newsweek .

"I would caution homeowners against thinking, 'a strong El Niño equals a wet winter everywhere.' I remember the 1997-98 winter as a very wet and stormy one for California, while 2015-16 was a very different story despite also being a strong El Niño," she said. "El Niño can point us toward a pattern, but it doesn't tell us exactly what every storm will do."

The southern tier of the U.S., including California, the Southwest, Texas, the Gulf Coast, and the Southeast, "tends to experience a wetter winter during El Niño," Emily J. Becker, deputy director at the Cooperative Institute for Marine & Atmospheric Studies (CIMAS) and Research Associate Professor at Rosenstiel School for Marine, Atmospheric & Earth Science, University of Miami, told Newsweek .

She added: "This impact is somewhat less reliable in California and more consistent through the Gulf Coast and Southeast.

"The East Coast also can experience a wetter winter. The Ohio River valley and the Pacific Northwest can be drier than average. Also, winter tends to be warmer through the northern central U.S. (and through much of Canada), especially earlier in the winter."

A stronger El Niño means these impacts are more likely to occur, but not necessarily likely to be extra-strong, according to experts.

Egger said that the southern half of the U.S. is where she would be watching most closely for the impact of El Niño, particularly California and the Southwest, the southern Rockies, and parts of the southern Plains and Gulf Coast.

She added: "A strong El Niño typically strengthens and shifts the Pacific jet farther south, which can support a more active storm track and increased precipitation across parts of the southern U.S.

"For California, the Sierra Nevada and other higher elevations are particularly important because that added moisture can translate into significant mountain snow when temperatures are cold enough. That snowpack is also critical to water supplies across the West."

Egger also noted she would be watching the southern Plains, Gulf Coast and Florida for an increased potential for severe storms, heavy rainfall and strong winds.

"The exact location and timing of those threats will depend on the individual weather pattern as we move through the season," she concluded.

articles.title: In 2018, billionaire pharma heir Frank Binder paid $33 million for a Hollywood Hills mansion; now the Lenny Kravitz-designed home is listed for $35 million as he builds a $2 billion residential yacht
articles.summary: US News: Swiss pharmaceutical heir and entrepreneur Frank Binder has listed his Hollywood Hills mansion for $35 million, eight years after buying the property..
articles.body: Swiss pharmaceutical heir and entrepreneur Frank Binder has listed his Hollywood Hills mansion for $35 million, eight years after buying the property. Binder, whose family made its fortune through Swiss pharmaceutical company Merck Serono, bought the mid-century modern home for $33 million in 2018, according to reports by the New York Post, AOL and Robb Report. The listing comes as Binder focuses on his biggest project yet: the construction of Ulyssia, a 323-metre, $2 billion mega-yacht designed as a floating residential community with 122 luxury apartments. Set on a hill overlooking the Sunset Strip and the wider Los Angeles basin, the 10,700-square-foot mansion offers wide views stretching from the city to the ocean. The property is located behind private security gates.Interior design by Kravitz Design and architectural detailsBuilt in 1964, the estate went through a major, multi-year renovation led by musician and designer Lenny Kravitz through his company Kravitz Design before Binder bought it. The redesign added a strong mid-century style, textured stone walls, custom wood panelling and floor-to-ceiling glass windows that bring in natural light and offer wide views of the Los Angeles skyline. The home has four bedrooms and seven bathrooms spread across several levels. Features include a commercial-grade kitchen with custom cabinets, a temperature-controlled wine cellar, a modern screening room and a large primary suite that opens directly onto private terraces overlooking the city. Outside, the property has a cantilevered infinity-edge swimming pool, an outdoor kitchen, fire pits and several covered lounge areas designed for entertaining.Shifting focus to a $2 billion residential ocean linerBinder’s decision to sell the Los Angeles home comes as he becomes more involved in Ulyssia, which is being promoted as the world’s largest and most advanced residential yacht. The 15-deck vessel is being built with China Merchants Cruise Shipbuilding, marine design company Deltamarin and naval architect Espen Øino. It is expected to begin sailing in 2030, according to Yacht Style and Boat International. The ship will have 122 permanent residences ranging from 110 to 1,600 square metres, with prices between €10 million and €100 million. Buyers must have a minimum net worth of $30 million to join the residential community. Planned facilities include a medical and wellness centre operated by Switzerland’s Chenot, two padel tennis courts, two helicopters, submersibles, seven restaurants, a school and a fully equipped marina bay.Binder, who founded Ulyssia Residences AG, plans to keep a 1,000-square-metre penthouse on the top deck, making the vessel his main home around the world.Real estate dynamics on the Sunset StripThe $35 million asking price reflects continued strength in the high-end Los Angeles property market, where luxury homes with celebrity connections and clear views remain attractive to wealthy international buyers. The property is represented by real estate agents Branden and Rayni Williams of The Beverly Hills Estates, along with Carl Gambino of Compass, according to real estate records cited by the New York Post. articles.title: Armed Ohio man arrested after charging at Democratic candidate for governor, Amy Acton
articles.summary: The candidate, Amy Acton, was not hurt, but her team said several others were injured as the man tried to "lunge" at her.
articles.body:
An armed man has been arrested in the US after charging towards Amy Acton, the Democratic politician campaigning to be Ohio state governor, during an event on Sunday.

The Ohio State Highway Patrol, who were working to protect Acton, told the BBC in a statement that its team had stopped the suspect before he reached Acton at Ohio's annual Canfield Fair event.

The suspect, identified as 38-year-old Patrick Havas, was carrying two pistols at the time of his arrest.

Acton herself was not injured during the incident , though her campaign team said several others were hurt as the man tried to "lunge" at her.

"Dr Acton and [her husband] Eric are grateful for the swift and decisive action of law enforcement and are praying for the recovery of those injured," a statement from her communications director said.

"This kind of violence has no place in Ohio. Dr Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another."

Giving some detail around the alleged incident, Mahoning County Sheriff Jerry Greene told the BBC's US partner CBS News that Havas, who was from Canfield, was arrested after he "aggressively shoved his way through the crowd toward Acton while holding a cell phone up".

He knocked over two people who were using mobility scooters, Greene added.

Havas is being held at the county jail and faces two counts of misdemeanor assault and one count of disorderly conduct.

Acton's Republican rival for the Ohio governor seat, Vivek Ramaswamy, an ally of US President Donald Trump, has condemned the incident.

Ramaswamy's own communications director said: "Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence. What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope that no-one was hurt."

The incumbent Ohio Governor, Republican Mike DeWine, similarly said there was no place for political violence at public events.

America has been rocked in recent years by numerous high-profile examples of political violence, with lawmakers being targeted in addition to attempts on Trump's life.

At times, the violence has been deadly. High-profile conservative activist Charlie Kirk was killed in Utah last September. Democratic state lawmaker Melissa Hortman and her husband were also killed at their home in Minnesota.

articles.title: Plans for major overhaul of councils halted
articles.summary: Proposals to merge smaller councils to form larger authorities have been paused or withdrawn in a number of areas.
articles.body:
Plans for a major shake-up of local government are on hold, after the government launched a review in light of new legal advice.

Proposals to merge smaller councils to form larger authorities in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk have been withdrawn.

Meanwhile, plans for 14 other areas will also be reviewed and paused.

Reorganisation in Surrey, where councillors for two new unitary authorities were elected in May, will not be affected by the review.

The government confirmed local elections in May 2027 would go ahead on existing council boundaries.

Confirming the review in Parliament, Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner told MPs that "in light of legal advice, I want to satisfy myself firstly that the right process is in place, that it is robust, and of course complies with the law".

She added: "And secondly, I want to fully test whether our proposals for local government reorganisation meet the priorities of a new administration and a new prime minister and any additional considerations."

Rayner acknowledged the announcement was "disappointing" but insisted the government was "determined more than ever to devolve power closer to the people we represent" - a key priority of new PM Andy Burnham.

The plans originated under Sir Keir Starmer's government, when Rayner was also local government secretary, before she was replaced by Steve Reed.

The government was already facing legal challenges over proposals to reorganise councils in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.

In June, Reform-led councils in Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk launched judicial reviews against the plans, while the Conservative-led administration in Hampshire did the same.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "Reform UK not only argued that this government's plans for local government reorganisation were an unmitigated disaster, but we once again put our money where our mouth is."

He added: "Thanks to our judicial reviews in affected Reform-led councils, the government has backed down on their plans yet again."

Conservative shadow local government minister David Simmonds said it was a "humiliation" for the government.

He said: "Ministers are only backing off because they have been found out in the face of relentless Conservative opposition to their gerrymandering."

Liberal Democrat local government spokeswoman Zöe Franklin said: "This is an embarrassing and chaotic climbdown, which has resulted in already cash-strapped councils wasting huge sums on plans the government told them were legally watertight."

Sean Matthews, from the County Councils Network, welcomed the move, adding: "Many of our members will be relieved that the decisions they viewed as damaging to local services and financially unsustainable have been withdrawn or are being reviewed."

A spokesperson for the Local Government Association, which represents councils, said that while local authorities hold different views on the reorganisation plans "there is no excuse for the government's mishandling of this process".

The spokesperson added that Rayner's announcement "will have caused significant uncertainty, after councils have invested scarce public money and countless hours" in the reorganisation programme.

Local government in England is currently covered by a complicated patchwork of arrangements.

In some places, responsibility for local services is shared between county councils, which manage areas including social care and education; and district councils, which cover smaller areas and are responsible for services such as bin collections.

Some areas, particularly larger towns and some cities, have "unitary" authorities responsible for both - while the regions surrounding big cities are increasingly covered by regional mayors and multi-council "combined" authorities, with greater powers in areas such as transport policy, planning and housing.

In late 2024, as local government secretary, Rayner announced plans to move towards unitary councils across all of England , with council boundaries redrawn and smaller district councils abolished.

The government argued the proposals would make the system simpler and produce savings by making the delivery of services more efficient, while also handing new powers from Westminster to regions across the country.

However, critics said the plans would not save money, while diverting resources from front-line services and leaving councils more remote from their communities.

Under Sir Keir, the government had been pushing ahead with the proposals.

In July – just days before Burnham became prime minister – Rayner's successor as secretary of state, Reed, had announced plans for new councils in 14 areas .

The 14 areas where local government reorganisation is being paused while a review is carried out are:

Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool

Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire

The government said decisions had not yet been taken on Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, and West Sussex, with these areas being considered alongside the wider review.

articles.title: Sam Smith and Chase & Status on Radio 1 Live Lounge line-up
articles.summary: Jorja Smith, Rachel Chinouriri and Blossoms also among artists set to take to the studio next month.
articles.body:
Sam Smith, Chase & Status and Jorja Smith are among the artists who have been revealed for BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge month.

Indie band Blossoms, singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri and US rappers Anderson .Paak and Cordae will also take to the studio in October.

Each Live Lounge guest traditionally performs an acoustic version of one of their own songs, plus a cover of a track by a different artist.

The sessions will air on Radio 1's Live Lounge show, which will now be fronted by Charlie Hedges and Jeremiah Asiamah.

The recordings will go out throughout October on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at midday on the pair's new show.

A performance from Stockport-formed band Blossoms on 5 October will kick off the run.

Rock band Nothing But Thieves, US rising star Stella Lefty, Brit-nominated singer Beabadoobee and London-based artist Odeal are also among the artists on the line-up.

Brighton duo Royal Blood will close out this year's sessions on 30 October, but a surprise artist, who will perform just before them, is still to be announced.

West Midlands superstar Jorja Smith will be performing following on from the release of her third album, What Are The Odds.

The Brit Award winner's latest album received largely positive reviews, with Rolling Stone UK describing it as her "best album yet".

Electronic heavyweights Chase & Status will also take to the studio after they headlined Reading and Leeds Festival last month.

And Oscar-winner Sam Smith will be rolling out their vocals following on from the release of their fifth album, Hazel Eyes, last month.

Hedges previously hosted the Live Lounge with fellow presenters Rickie Haywood-Williams and Melvin Odoom, who have since left the station as part of a major schedule shake-up.

In an Instagram post at the time, Hedges said she was "so excited" to host the show alongside Asiamah and sent her support to her former colleagues, saying she would be "cheering them on in their next chapter".

Following the Live Lounge announcement, Asiamah said it is a "privilege" to take on the role and host the upcoming line-up of guests.

"Bring it on. Hope you're ready, because I ain't, it's going to be a surprise and a big vibe," he added.

Wednesday 7 October - Nothing But Thieves

Wednesday 21 October - Rachel Chinouriri

Monday 26 October - Anderson .Paak x Cordae

Wednesday 28 October – To be revealed soon

articles.title: Constable painting draws crowds in his home county of Suffolk
articles.summary: The Hay Wain depicts a rural scene in Suffolk and is on show there for the first time.
articles.body:
A famous John Constable painting has been viewed by more than 11,000 people since it went on display in the county it depicts for the first time.

The Hay Wain, an 1821 oil painting of a rural scene near the River Stour in Flatford, Suffolk, was unveiled at Ipswich's Christchurch Mansion two months ago.

It will remain there until 4 October, having been loaned to Colchester and Ipswich Museums from the National Gallery in London.

Ipswich Borough Council described its appearance in the county as a "once-in-a-generation" occasion.

Constable was born in 1776 in East Bergholt and produced many paintings of the Suffolk countryside during his career, until his death in 1837, aged 60.

His works helped to give the area the nickname Constable Country, but The Hay Wain was actually produced in London.

The exhibition in Ipswich - which also celebrates the artist's life and other works - is part of a series of celebrations to mark the 250th anniversary of his birth.

articles.title: Yemen gov’t forces launch air strikes on Houthi targets
articles.summary: The Houthis and Yemeni government forces are battling for control of the critical Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
articles.body:
Yemeni government forces say they have carried out air strikes on Houthi positions across the country as the Iran-aligned group claims it shot down several Saudi drones.

“The armed forces’ warplanes carried out raids targeting Houthi militia positions in al-Barah, south of Hodeidah and in the western outskirts of Marib. They also targeted sites and gatherings of the militia in al-Lubnat, al-Alam and al-Jawf governorate centre, and inflicted heavy loss of life and equipment on the militia,” the military said in a statement late on Sunday.

Yahya Saree, the Houthis’ military spokesperson, said on Monday that Houthi fighters shot down three Saudi drones in the past 24 hours.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi Arabia on the claims.

Saree said the group’s forces shot down a Saudi CH-4 armed reconnaissance drone over al-Jawf province as it was carrying out “hostile activities”. He later added that a Saudi-owned Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone was shot down in al-Bayda governorate.

The Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and have carried out attacks on Saudi shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

The Houthis and government forces have been fighting over control of the critical waterway that has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports since Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz in response to the US-Israel war on Iran launched in February.

On Friday, Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a series of air strikes against several Houthi positions in the country, as the Houthis attempted to advance through western Taiz and southern Hodeidah towards al-Makha (Mocha) and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

articles.title: Space wars are no longer science fiction: How nations are preparing for conflict in orbit
articles.summary: International News: Space, often called the final frontier, is fast becoming central to how wars will be fought on the planet. From communication to guiding weapons onto .
articles.body: Space, often called the final frontier, is fast becoming central to how wars will be fought on the planet. From communication to guiding weapons onto the cap of a bottle to keeping the adversary under persistent observation, a lot of critical opportunities are now permanently on orbit. From the earliest days of combat, the importance of high ground has been well understood. This high ground has been moving higher and is now well established in space. With nations continuously strengthening their space-based capabilities. Even India is planning to have a constellation of 52 satellites up in space by 2029. These satellites will provide the Indian armed forces a continuous set of eyes in the sky, provide secure communications and improve the situational awareness for commanders. The assets established in this new high ground will cut through what for centuries has been known as the fog of war.This dependence on space-based assets is only growing, with more capabilities now being put in orbit. The more widespread use of precision weapons and now the increasing use of autonomous systems has increased the dependence on satellites for the purpose of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT). Increasingly, as the nature of combat moves towards a network-centric environment, this new paradigm primarily differs from the previous modes as it depends more openly on different systems located at various locations to form a common battlefield picture in which the sensors and shooters talk to each other automatically. In such a large design, satellites provide an invisible thread to a large number of nodes in a massive web of assets that could be spread across hundreds of kilometers. Satellites provide the most efficient solution of keeping all systems in the same information network. Before this new pattern, militaries relied on linear kill chains, which were rigid and linear, the destruction or neutralisation of a single element in this paradigm would put an end to the entire operation.One effective way to degrade a kill web would be to neutralise or destroy satellites that are instrumental in bearing the weight of the entire network. This is easier said than done. Four countries, including India, apart from the US, China and Russia, possess the capability to take down satellites of hostile nations.Treaty governing warfare in spaceThe era of space exploration is closely intertwined with the Cold War between the United States, which led NATO, and the Soviet Union, which formed the Warsaw Pact. From before the launch of he very first satellite, both sides of the Iron Curtain were looking at ways to weaponise the last frontier. As the danger of weaponizing became clear to both sides, it was decided to limit the use of the black skies of space to bring darkness to Earth. In 1967 Russia and the US, just a decade after the launch of the first satellite—Sputnik—signed the Outer Space Treaty, formally called the Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies. 118 countries, including India and China, are parties to the agreement, while another 20 nations are signatories to this critical multinational agreement.The Outer Space Treaty bars nuclear weapons in space and reserves the Moon and other celestial bodies strictly for peaceful use. It establishes space as free for exploration by all nations and blocks any country from claiming sovereignty over it. This also hurts Donald Trump's claim to the moon, as the US is a party to the agreement found under the auspices of the United Nation. Military bases, weapons testing and manoeuvres on celestial bodies are explicitly prohibited. Notably, though, the treaty does not ban all military activity in space. It also does not prevent nations from setting up military space forces or deploying conventional weapons in orbit.It is important that a nation has the capability to bring down a satellite, however this is not a capability that one should use lightly. As the entire civil aviation architecture, the entire sea lane of communications, mobile phones spectrum and a host of other critical links needed for critical tasks are dependent on satellites. So the shooting down of a satellite could hamper these networks functioning. So, the capability is very important, but it is not to be used lightly.The act of destructionFind, fix and finish, this as the name suggests is how militaries define the three stages of destroying a target. Find as the name suggests is the first step, this phase is linked to identification and initial detection of a target. The process here relies on intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance to discover where the target is located. Once the position of a target is identified, the next step is to fix the target, this means pinpointing the target's exact position with high accuracy and locking down its movement. The terminal step oof this stage act is called - finish. In this phase the actual violent act of firing the weapon to neutralise or destroy the target.In terms of satellites, these tasks get progressively more difficult as one moves through the sequence. Finding a satellite being the easiest phase as satellites are continuously monitored as our their orbits. This is done due to deconflicting. As thousands of satellites are now in space, it becomes imperative to keep the space deconflicted as a collision between two objects each flying through space at speeds measured in thousands of kilometers per hour could create a large debris field that could affect even more satellites. For this reason the movement of all satellites is tracked by space agencies. The known orbits of a satellite helps in tracking and accurately predicting the position of these objects, thereby taking care of the find and fix element.Finish on the other hand is the most difficult task and only four countries have this advanced capability. Space is fast turning into a contested battlefield, and the tools of anti-satellite warfare are already being tested in real conflicts. The Ukraine war opened with a cyberattack on the Viasat satellite network hours before Russian tanks rolled in, degrading Kyiv's military communications before a single shot was fired on the ground. Jamming and spoofing have since become routine on that battlefield, with China and Iran both fielding jammers, and low-powered GPS jammers now available for a few dollars online. Satellites in the geo-synchronous orbit are out of reach of most ground based anti-satellite weapons, but are deadly to objects in the low earth orbit.Kinetic ASAT weapons remain the most destructive option on the table. China's 2007 missile test on a dead weather satellite created thousands of debris fragments expected to linger in orbit for seven decades, prompting America's own Operation Burnt Frost the following year. Any nation with basic missile and tracking capability, even Iran or North Korea, could theoretically strike a satellite given how predictable orbital paths are.Equally worrying are co-orbital satellites like Russia's Luch-1 and Luch-2, which have made suspicious close approaches to other spacecraft. The larger fear underpinning all this is Kessler Syndrome, a scenario where cascading collisions generate so much orbital debris that entire swathes of space become unusable, threatening the satellite-dependent global economy itself.As reported by ToI in May last year, India too ran a sophisticated space "dogfight," with a chaser and target satellite conducting coordinated, close-range manoeuvres nearly 500 kilometres above Earth, an extension of ISRO's SPADEX mission. The exercise followed China's own satellite dogfighting tests in low Earth orbit back in 2024. Travelling at 28,800 kilometres per hour, some 28 times faster than a commercial jet and ten times the speed of a bullet, the two satellites autonomously executed rendezvous and proximity manoeuvres, essentially practising the delicate choreography of approaching, tracking and manoeuvring around each other in orbit, a capability with clear strategic as well as societal applications for India's growing space programme.ISRO laid the groundwork for protecting India's space assets back in August 2019, when it laid the foundation stone for a Space Situational Awareness Control Centre in Bengaluru. Built around NETRA, the Network for Space Object Tracking and Analysis, at the ISTRAC campus in Peenya, the facility combined radars and telescopes to monitor and track debris and potential threats to Indian satellites. The setup included a sophisticated multi-object tracking radar in Nellore, another in Northeast India, and telescopes in Thiruvananthapuram, Mount Abu and North India, covering all directions of approach.Crucially, the network was designed to reduce India's reliance on the US-run NORAD for space situational awareness data. A related Space Situational Awareness Data Sharing pact with the US, signed later in 2022, allowed ISRO to collaborate directly with America's Combined Space Operations Center to safeguard both countries' satellites from natural and man-made threats. The move reflected ISRO's growing recognition that with more assets in orbit, India needed its own independent capability to detect and respond to collisions, debris and hostile activity in space as the new high ground will dictate how wars are fought on the surface.

articles.title: Make AI-merica Great Again: Meme Lord Donald Trump’s digital feed goes off rails again
articles.summary: US News: TOI correspondant from Washington: Somewhere between George Washington on horseback, a lunar conquest, and another imaginary demolition of Iran’s Khar.
articles.body: TOI correspondant from Washington: Somewhere between George Washington on horseback, a lunar conquest, and another imaginary demolition of Iran’s Kharg Island, the United States Presidency appeared to relocate from the White House to an AI image generator for several hours on Sunday.MAGA boss Donald Trump spent much of Sunday evening at his golf resort in Bedminster, New Jersey, conducting what can only be described as a digital variety show on Truth Social, unleashing a 37-post torrent of AI-generated images, videos, boasts, insults, and proposed geographic renovations. The performance ranged from the merely self-congratulatory and narcissistic to the geopolitically consequential – sometimes within the same minute.A review of Trump's posts shows the afternoon descending into a surreal collage of AI slop: Trump meeting George Washington at the White House, Trump riding with him, Trump appearing at McDonald's, Trump as Hulk Hogan, Trump surrounded by robots, and Trump standing beside a television displaying an edited image of Joe Biden.There was also a Space Force launched nuclear conflagration, a lunar image proclaiming, “The Moon Is Ours,” and a suggestion that New Mexico – a Pueblo nation that predates both the USA and Mexico – might henceforth be known as “New America.”Turning his attention to Iran, Trump imposed his face on the country and posted an AI-generated image involving demolition of Kharg Island.Trump's previous AI depiction of its Kharg Island’s destruction prompted administration officials to explain it was intended as a message rather than an announcement of an actual US strike.That distinction – between a meme, a threat, a joke, and government policy — is now becoming increasingly difficult to maintain amid Trump’s social media mayhem. Sunday's posts arrived amid renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran is threatening additional restrictions after the US ramped up military pressure.Reuters reported Monday that Iran planned to announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf, while oil flows through the waterway remains a major source of global concern. So when the US president posts something about the Strait of Hormuz, the world is having a hard time determining whether it is comedy, propaganda, psychological warfare or an actual policy signal.At home, critics have been quick to interpret the Trump barrage of AI slop with alarm, some describing the latest outpouring as another “mental health episode” that calls for invoking the 25th Amendment, a constitutional mechanism to remove the President in the event of incapacity.Its involuntary provisions require the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet to act, followed by a two-thirds vote of both chambers of Congress to remove the president if he contests the determination.No one seriously expects this to happen although the British Medical Journal reported in May that 30 US mental-health specialists had signed a statement declaring Trump mentally unfit for office and citing what they regarded as observable concerns about cognition, judgment and impulse control.But there is another interpretation of the President’s digital excesses: The Trump White House has increasingly operated as a social-media and influencer machine, using memes, videos and rapid-response posts to “drown out” opponents, generate viral attention, and overwhelm conventional news coverage.Trump's defenders, in this interpretation, have portrayed his posts as trolling, baiting opponents, entertaining supporters and “keeping everyone else guessing.”But the problem, many analysts argue, is that the US President possesses something internet trolls do not: nuclear weapons, a powerful military, shadowy intelligence agencies, and the ability to move markets with a sentence. “It’s time to stop making excuses for President Trump, claiming that everything is a joke.“Joking” about choosing to launch nuclear war is evidence of dangerous detachment from any basic level of understanding his job,” one military vet raged on X.“It is time to acknowledge President Trump is suffering serious cognitive decline. We allow this to go on unchecked to our collective peril. If we don’t take constitutional measures to correct this deficiency while there is still time, we may invite destruction on ourselves,” he added.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
